title: Overlapping remote syncs can make an older Grist snapshot the head

evidence.quote: const result = this.store.commit(doc.path, bytes, model, { message: 'Synced from Grist' });

reasoning: The poller starts a new sync every 15 seconds without checking whether the previous sync is still in flight, and the UI can start a manual sync at the same time. Each sync commits whatever bytes it fetched when it resolves. If an older request is slow and a newer request commits first, the older response can commit afterward and become the latest head, making the remote history appear to regress.
reproduction: Use a mock Grist server where sync A returns old bytes after a delay and sync B returns newer bytes quickly. Start two syncRemote calls concurrently; B commits new content, then A commits old content as the latest version.
recommendation: Serialize syncRemote per document with an in-flight promise/mutex, or tag fetches and discard stale completions when a newer sync has already committed. Also avoid setInterval overlap by awaiting or skipping when a sync is running.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The smoke test covers connect and one later sync sequentially; it never overlaps poller/manual sync calls or controls response ordering.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a service test with a delayed mock Grist server that resolves two concurrent syncs out of order and asserts the branch head remains on the newest snapshot.
